questions.question: When does a motorcycle have less traction for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as in a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Hides you from other road users.
Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
To look for dark clouds that may show bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to see vehicles coming from behind. Make sure drivers see you and respond to your actions when you stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: The front tire affects steering and balance.
A flat front tire disables the front brake.
A flat front tire stops you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire affects steering and balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering hard, which affects your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must:

options.text: Limit your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before entering a turn. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to leave your lane or go off the road.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: They are less dangerous than using either alone.
Their effects can be stronger than using either alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects can be stronger than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist stop quickly?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Look ahead on the road to help you avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: Which color will make you less visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: What is a benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you more time to respond to dangers and more room to move safely.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time?

options.text: Just start riding. You learn best by doing.
Just start riding. Most bikes are the same.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every bike is different. Before riding, check the bike's safety and maintenance. Find where everything is. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how it works.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands before riding.

questions.question: If you have been drinking alcohol, what should you do?

options.text: Ride if you think you are not impaired.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking alcohol. Even small amounts can be unsafe.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, how does your ability to ride safely change?
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist reduce the chance of a collision?

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road in front of the motorcycle.
Refuse to move to avoid a hazard.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds along your path of travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds along your path of travel.
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and be seen.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and surface hazards. It also discourages sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield does not provide the same protection as a good face shield.

questions.question: What should you usually do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by causing them to tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time will help your body remove alcohol. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take before riding ability is affected?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can hurt your ability to safely ride. Never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and warn drivers about road conditions. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
Clothing that does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash while keeping you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: Why is it hard to ride right after rain starts?

options.text: Some drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.explanation: Just after rain starts, the pavement is especially slippery. Oil from vehicles mixes with water before it washes away, creating a slippery surface.

questions.question: What helps you avoid serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense against injury while riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and warn drivers about road conditions. This sign warns that the road ahead is likely to be slippery when wet.
